FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides Residue Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Dicofol formulations insecticidal activity. are used in agriculture for the control of mites. It is a non-systemic acaricide with little Although residues in soil decrease rapidly, traces may remain for more than one year.

In the preparation of this standard due consideration has been given to the limits of dicofol residues laid down under the provisions of Prevention qf Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rules framed thereunder. This standard will enable the food, health authorities and others engaged in the field to follow uniform test procedures for the estimation of dicofol and its major metabolite 4,4 - dichlorobenzophenone residues in various agricultural food commodities and soil. In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (reyised)`.

METHODFORDETERMINATIONOFDICOFOL RESIDUESINAGRICULTURALANDFOOD COMMODITIES
1 SCOPE This standard prescribes the gas chromatographic method for the determination of dicofol [2,2,2 trichloro - I, I - bis(4- chlorophenyl) ethanol] and its major metabolite 4,4'- dichlorobenzophenone residues in agricultural, food commodities and soil.

3 SAMPLING The representative samples for the purpose estimating dicofol residues shall be drawn accordance'with IS 11380 (Part 1). 4 APPARATUS 4.1 Waring Blender 4.2 Kuderna-Danish 4.3 Centrifuge bottles. Evaporator with 250 ml capacity centrifuge of in

6 EXTRACTION 6.1 Crop Samples Transfer a suitable quantity (100-200 g) of finely chopped crop sample into the blender jar. Add IO-50 g of anhydrous sodium sulphate followed by n-hexane keeping the sample-solvent ratio at I:2 (w/vi. Blend at high speed for 3-5 minutes. Filter the mixture through a funnel fitted with a permanent filter of the porosity rated as I. Wash the blender jar twice with

2 mm aperture size. 45 cm long and 2.0 cm in dia.

4.7 Glass Column 4.8 Hot Air-Oven 4.9 Water Bath

IS 14629 : 1999 50 ml of n-hexane. Combine the filtrate and washing. Concentrate the aliquot on steam bath with Kuderna-Danish evaporator. Traces can be removed at room temperature by passing a gentle stream of air. 6.2 Milk Samples 6.2.1 Either 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.1.2 may be followed for extraction of the pesticide in milk samples. 6.2.1.1 Place 100 ml of milk in a 250 ml centrifuge bottle. Add 30 ml potassium oxalate solution and warm to about 45'C on a water bath. Add IO ml aqueous mixture of Triton X-45, mix thoroughly and maintain at 45OC for 20 minutes. Cool to room temperature. Centrifuge to obtain a clear fat layer and add 100 ml of n-hexane. Stopper and shake the bottle gently to gather the fat layer. Centrifuge until the n-hexane layer is clear. Remove the n-hexane layer without disturbing the milky phase. To wash over the n-hexane left behind, slowly add another 100 ml of n- hexane (do not disturb the milky phase), separate and add to the first extract. Give one more washing and combine all the extracts. Filter the extract in Kuderna-Danish evaporator and concentrate under the a nitrogen atmosphere to dryness (or fatty residues). 6.2.1.2 Add acetone to 100 ml of milk which will result in coarse precipitation of milk solids. Remove the solids by filtering through glass wool. Take the filterate in a separatory funnel and extract the pesticide twice with 100 ml of petroleum ether each time. Combine the extracts and concentrate it on water bath. 6.3 Animal Tissue Place a 50 g sample of animal tissue in a blender. Add enough anhydrous sodium sulphate to absorb water present in tissues. Add 200 ml of n-hexane and blend fur 5 minutes. Pour the extract in centrifuge bottle, rinsing the biender jar with SO ml of n- hexane and add to centrifuge bottle. Centrifuge for 5 minutes at about 1 500 rpm. Separate the n-hexane layer and concentrate (use 50 ml of n-hrxdne to rinse centrifuge tubes). 6.4 Tea Sample Take 50 g of tea and extract by blending with 150 ml n-hexane in a Waring blender for 10 minutes. The extract is filtered through Buchner funnel with Whatman No. 41 filter paper. The filtrate thus obtained is then concentrated to IO ml with the help of a rotary vacuum evaporator. The concentrate is freed from moisture with anhydrous sodium sulphate. 6.5 Urine Sample Take 20 ml of urine in a separatory funnel and add 100 ml of acetonitrilc and 50 ml of distilled water. Extract the mixture 3 times with 000 ml rl-hexune each time. Combine the extractions and evaporate the solvents at 40�C on a rotary evaporator. 2
7

CLEANUP

7.1 Paitk a glass column to a height of about 5 cm with florisil. The column shall be saturated with petroleum ether. Add the sample extract to this column the gradually. elute Thereafter, PPdichlorobenzophenone using a mixture 15 ml of ether and 135 ml of n-hexane. Finally, elute the pp-dicofol using a mixture containing 35 ml of ether and 115 ml of n-hexane. The flow should be regulated at about 2 ml per minute with the help of a rubber cork.
NOTE This method helps to separate all the important metabolites in a mixture except of course pp' dicofol and pp' dichlorobenzophenone @p' dicofol is converted into pp' dichlorobenzophenonc immediately after injecting in gas chromatograph). The only known and emy solution to the problem is the use of a florisil column to separate those two compounds prior to column injection. For eluting pp' dicofol use eluting mixture of 35 ml ether and I15 ml of n-hexane whereas for eluting pp' dichlorobenzophenone a mixture of 15 ml ether and 135 ml n- hexane may be used.

7.2 Tea samples are cleaned up by passing through an absorbant column packed with 20 g of activated florisil. The column is elute with a mixture of 10 percent diethyl ether in n-hexane (200 ml). Finally the column elute is evaporated to dryness and the final volume is made up to 10 ml with n-hexane. 8 ESTIMATION 8.1 Principie 8.1.1 The dicofol residue extracted from the sample is measured gas chromatographically using an electron capture detector. The content of dicofol is determined by comparing the response with a reference standard of dicofol. 8.2 Gas Chromatograph 8.2.1 A gas chromatograph equipped with an electron capture detector used for the separation and estimation of dicofol from extracts. After injecting the GLC column gets converted to corresponding ketone, which elutes from the column and gives a well defined peak. The area of ketone peak is used for quantification purpose under the following suggested conditions. The parameters may be changed according to the available facilities, provided standardization is done.
